terra.problem: Saying Paul knows the next part matters assigns him an unstated thought and reason for continuing.
“Whatever was said in Paradise stays there” goes beyond the text. Paul says the things the man heard were not permitted to be told, not that nothing said there could be shared.
Calling Paul's weaknesses “the bloopers” suggests mistakes, which the passage does not say they were.
The comparison to power coming with a big shiny stamper does not have a clear connection to the point being made.
Saying Paul isn't grumbling about his weaknesses anymore implies that he was grumbling before. The passage does not say that.
The passage connects Paul's weakness and strength with Christ's power, but it does not say that Paul's strength isn't his own.
Saying Paul doesn't end up alone asserts something the passage does not address.
